lines.text: How does DoorDash pick which driver gets your order?
The closest driver isn't always best. Food takes time to cook, and nearby orders can share a trip.
lines.title: Not just distance

lines.text: The old single program struggled. At peak, demand reached nearly four times what it could handle.
lines.title: Old engine at peak

lines.text: So DoorDash split the job. A coordinator tracks the situation and hands heavy math to many workers.
lines.title: Boss and workers

lines.text: Each worker gets only the local data it needs, and a final step joins the answers across borders.
lines.title: Key ideas

lines.text: Before going live, the new engine ran in shadow mode, making decisions that were only recorded.
lines.title: Safe rollout

lines.text: The result: ten times the processing scale, and over 99.96 percent of runs finished in under 20 seconds.
lines.title: Results

lines.text: The lesson: to scale, split the problem sensibly, not just add servers.
lines.title: Takeaways
